### 1711509 Flushing radiator

If oil has entered the coolant circuit,theradiator and expansion tank must be flushed and cleaned with Solvethane\*\*cleaning agent.

Follow the procedure described below:

1. Removing and installing the radiator. see1711000. Removing and installing or replacing coolant expansion tank,see 17 11100.   
2. Fill with approx.2 liters of Solvethane.   
3. Shake radiator and tank well, then empty once the oil has separated.   
4. Reinstallthe cleaned radiator and expansion tank and connect to the cooling circuit.   
5. Fill the entire cooling circuit with hot water and flush, if necessary severaltimes,to be sure of clearing the system of any cleaning residue.   
6. Check drained coolant for oil residue and,if necessary,repeat process5. After the cleaning operation,fill the coolingsystem. Bleed the cooling system and check for leakage, see.1700039.


### Comment:

Solvethane attacks rubber seale, hoses etc. and must therefore not be allowed to enter the cooling circuit, orto remain there.For thls reason, always follow the safety regulations governing the use of Solvethane (printed on the containers).

### Checking Deflection Angle of Propeller Shaft:

### Centering Propeller Shaft:

Loosen exhaust assembly,engine rubber mounts and transmisslon cross member.

Apply Speclal Tool 26 4 020.

Set the Indicator perpendicular with help of the water scale. Read degrees.

Note:   
Always apply the speclal tool with the scale in the same direction (e.g.scale right).   
One graduation = 5'.   
The position of the car is not important,since only separate angles are compared.

Appllcation Points: Bore In engine carrier atrear.

Manual Transmission: I cast rib at center

Automatic Transmission: 1 center bolt of transmission extenslon

Punch mark measuring points.

### Toe Dlfference Angle

Is the angle, by which the king pin\*is Inclined Inward froma perpendicular lIne to the lateral axls of the car. The klngpin Inclination produces returning forces, whlch retum theroad wheels and steering wheel to straight aheadafter driving through a curve or around a corner.


### King Pin Inclination

is the angular position of the wheel on the Inside ofacurve to thewheel on the outslde ofa curve when driving in acurve. The steering is designed that the angular position o the wheels changes as steering lock progresses. The toe difference angle provides Informatlon on thepertinent operation of thesteering trapezoid for leftorright steering lock from the center position. A correctly adjusted toe difference angle-produces equal values for left and rlght lock Indue conslderatlon for factory manufacturing tolerances.

a =Toe difference angle D = Turning circle centerpoint

![](images/1d0275876d9f11888095110b0568519e4ca7e7219717501a16914321fd592d36.webp)

Camber and kingpin inclination determine the location of the wheel contact polnt with the road surface. Kingpin inclinationreduces theleverage, on which frictional forcesare engaged, whlch makes 1t easler to turn the wheels to left orright lock. In addlton,thejolts fromroughroad surfacesdonot have as strong Influence on thesteering.

The "king pin"is equal to a line through the center polnt of the spring strut mount and control arm ball joint.

### Caster

Isthe inclinatlon of the king pin\* In forward direction asseen from the side.

The wheels arepulled and not pushed because of caster. Ina similar manner to king pin inclination, when driving In curves or around cornersreturning forcesare produced tohelp return the wheels to stralght ahead position.

The"king pin"Is equal to aline through the center point of the spring strut mount and control arm ball jolnt.

### Wheel Offset

is the angle, by whlch onefront wheel isdisplaced more toward front or rear than the other front wheel.

### Geometrical Axis1

is the bisecting line of anangle from the total rear wheel toe. Front wheel measurements are taken In reference to this axis.


### Symmetrlcal Axls2

is a center line running through the front and rear axles.

H 公 nut is tightened down more than 5 times during the adjustment check,it must be replaced -theself-locking characteristics   
become too impaired.

### Components:

Basic airbag unit, EEC Central airbag unit US (under the oddments tray beside the handbrake lever)

Steering wheel with airbag unit (airbag, gas generator. ignition squib and contact ring).

Airbag indicator lamp in the instrument cluster)

Passenger airbag unit (airbag, gas generator, ignition squib )

Knee guard (US model)


### Function

The system is triggered by sensors when vehicle retardation is equivalent to a direct head-on collision at no less than 18km/h with a solid obstacle (i.e.one which does not yield).

This closes the circuit,igniting the gas generators.This sudden combustion causes non-toxic gases to be released by the solid fuel mixture. These completely inflate the folded airbag in the steering wheeland instrument panel within the space of approx. 30ms. Whenfully inflated,the airbagminimizes injuries to headand upper torso in head-oncollisions. Discharging takes place through two holes on the side of the airbag facing away from the driver/ passenger.

Monitoring:

The alrbag system is monitored continuously by a diagnosing unit from ignition lock position"1". The control lamp comes on and goes out again after about 6 seconds to indicate that the system is ready for use.

I this lamp comes on again, there is a detected fault in the system.   
Sell -diagnosis -interrogate the faultmemorywith the BMW DIAGNOSING SYSTEM.   
Airbaglltroubleshootingrefer toRepair Instructions for 3 Series E36.

### BREAKING-IN PROCEDURES AFTER REPLACING/REPAIRING FINAL DRIVE

Sirict conformance wlth these breaking-in procedures Is requlred for preloading the tapered roller bearing.

During theflrst 1,0ookm thecar must be driven at difterent engine speeds and road speeds, but never fasterthan 2/3rds of the max. perml: ssible speed.

If thore is no conformance wlth these breaking-In procedures there could be selzure betwoen the tapered rollers and Inner race guide band, which in turn wlll continuously cause nolse,overheating and oll leakage.

Install a label or tag to remind thedriver of the breaking-in speclflcallons and next oll change.

### Installation:

Place round wire snap ring (1) in groove of final drive case prior to installation and in such a manner that both ends of ring are recessed in groove.   
This prevents lateral bending of the ring. Turn in drive flange by hand with light pressure until the round wire snap ring is heard to engage.

333 450 (cover with 8 screws)or   
333420 (cover with6 screws).   
Replace drive flange if the bearing surface is seriously scored.

### ACTIVE REAR AXLEKINEMATIC (AHK)

In comparison with conventional rear axles, active rear axle kinematic makes 1 possible to actively control the'bulld-up of lateral force on the rear axleby way of selective sleering..Thls conslderablyreduces thehazard of swerving.


### Example:

In case of a sudden obstacle avoldance maneuver (panic steering) normally steered vehicleswillreact wlth swervingmotion under certain conditions, which can even be ampllfled by"correcting onthe steoring wheel"   
The occurring tendency toswerving lsreduced conslderably under certaln conditlons In vehlcles with AHK.


### Deslgn:

Input varlables of the system are steering wheel angle and road speed. They are measured twlce(redundanl) in the Interest of driving safety.An electronic control unlt also fitted with redundant mlcroprocessors calculates an oplimal steering angle for the rearwheels depending on the pertinent driving condltlon.   
Correcllons arecarled out byanelectric/hydraulicdrive unit.Thedrive unlt isImme dlately arrested by hydraulic/mechanical clamps In case ol serlous systemdisturbance. Rearwheelsare brought to and arrested In stralght ahead position In case ol less serlous dlsturbance.   
In otherwords, driving salety lsnever lmpalred.   
The dlsturbance ls always reported to the drlver by a warninglamp in the Instrument cluster.


### Self-test:

The AHK system actlvates a sellf-test alter each engine start to check the operalion o1 electric,hydraulic and mechanlcal components.   
The mechanical clamp of the setting cyllnder,among others,Is brlellyactivated on ihe drlve unlt.   
Swltching themechanical clamp on and olf produces a "pounding sound"which mlght bo heard In the passenger compartment.   
Atter concluslon ol the sell-test the AHK system ls actlve;but the AHK system remalns Inactlve lf a fault is recognlzed.

The brake system is one of the most important safety systems on a motor vehicle. For this reason,particular care must be takenwith all work on the brake system and account should be taken of the following points:

The brake fluid must be replaced at least every two years.   
Caution:never reuse drained brake fluid.   
Brake fluid must not be poured down drains,onto open ground or into systems not suited to this substance. There is an inherent risk of contaminating ground water because brake fluid is listed as a.water source contaminant.   
Brake disks must not be scored or cracked and,in addition, minimum disk thickness,disk runout,parallelism and surface roughness of friction faces must not fall above or below specified values. Brake drumsmust not be out of roundness,scored or cracked. Brake lining thickness must not fall below the specified minimum level\*. Always replace brake disks, brake drums and brake linings inpairs(i.e.either side of same axle).   
Only loosen or tighten screw connections on brake pipes with a special brake pipe wrench (this avoids damage tothepipes).   
Whendismantling the brake system,seal allbrake pipes and individual components to prevent particles of dirtfromentering the brake system.Ensure unitis kept clean and always use non-fluffing cloths.   
All moving parts in the brake system must move easily (adjustment fixtures,brake caliper guides, handbrake cables and actuation).   
Afterevery operation on the brake system. it must be bled. This should be followed by a low pressure and a high pressure test.   
On vehicles with ASC+T,also performa"brake application function test.   
Check all connecting parts for leakage.   
Oilsor grease must not enter the brake system under any circumstances since these destroy all rubber components and can cause the brake system to fail.   
When cleaning brake components (with brake cleaning fluid), brake cleaning fluid must never be allowed to enter the brake system.   
Thechlorinated hydrocarbonsfrequently contained in brake cleaning fiuids lead to corrosion of brake components.

When repairing brake calipers, only use approved, glycol-based assembly compounds.

Brake pipes and hoses must be routed correctly and must not make contact with other parts or chafe at any point.   
lfthe system is bled using a bleeding device,always follow the manufacturer's operating instructions.   
Do not allow brake fluid to make contact with the paint on the vehicle. Brake fiuid damages the paintwork.   
Wash off brake dust or remove with suction: do not blow away with compressed air.   
Brake linig dust is a health hazard!   
If brake fluid enters theeyes,flush immediately with large quantities offresh water lf eyes are irritated,seek appropriate medical attention without delay.   
To avoid damage to theskin,keep contact timeof brakefluid on the skinas short as possible. Use soap and water to clean skin coated with brake fluid.


### 34 00 015 CHECKING BRAKE BOOSTING SYSTEM

Discharge the hydraulic reservolr by operating the brake pedal about 20 times wlth ihe engine stopped and a force equal 10 tull stop braking.   
Pull off wires and unscrew hydraullc pressure swltch.   
Mount Speclal Tools34 3 160 and 32 4005.

InstaNafion: Tightening torque\*.

Connect pressure tester (Speclal Tool 32 4000 or alternatlvely 54 3 100）to Speclal Tools 343 160 and 32 4005.

I the reservolr pressure (pressure gage) drops by more than5 bar wlthin 5mlnutes, disconnect the return plpe at the power flow regulator.

Ileak oll runs out of the return plpe bore in the power flow regulator, the power llow regulator leaks and must be replaced. 1 no leak oll runs out and the reservolr pressure stll drops,the brake booster has an Internal leak and must be replaced.

Hydraulic Reservolr Functlon Test: Operate the brake pedal about 20 tmes to drop the reservolr pressure (pressure gage) to zero. Start engine and observe the pressure gage. ### AUTOMATIC STABILITY CONTROL AND TRACTION {ASC +T

Purpose of ASC +T:

Easler moving off for drlver   
Guarantee of directional stablllty and steerability   
Improvement of traction {+ T   
Information fordriver

Description of Operation:

The system has the task ol regulating the slip of driven wheels to the lowest possible value regardless of theroad surface condition.

Engine torque ls reduced vla DME(ignition timing correction) and EML(throttle valve correction) during regulation. 1 thisis not sufficlent,the drive wheel rotating too fast wlll be slowed down by the wheel brake vla a hydraullc element of the plunger hydraulic unit.

The system ls swltched on automatically after starting the engine and can be swltched off manually. The ASC lamp is off with the system switched on.

The ASC lamp In the instrument cluster flashes to Inform the driver when regulatlon has been activated.   
Ifthe ASC lamp ls on continuously, the system was switched off automatically because of a fault orwas switched offmanually.

Note:

Troubleshooting ■ see Car Electric/Electronic Test Plan.

Important!

Pull off the ASC + Tcontrol unlt plug before starting the engine for theflrst time after working on the oll supply tank, tandem pump, high pressure filter, ASC+Thydraulic control unit and corresponding connectlon lines. Reconnect control unit plug with the Ignition turned off after the engine has run 1 minute.

Swltch ot ASC+T when testing ona brake roller test stand pr dynamometer test stand!

### DESCRIPTION OF BRAKE MASTERCYLINDER OPERATION

The operating forceapplied on push rod piston （8） produces hydraullic braking pressure in the first pressure chamberof the tandem master cylinderand the connected brake circult 1. ### DESCRIPTION

The basis of a braking action is the friction between the tires and road surlace. To brake a vehicle the tires have to transmlt a frlctlonal forceto theroad surface. In So dolng there wll be slip between the tiresandroad surface, l.e.the tire peripheral velocitywll be slower than the road speed of the vehicle.

Figure73034112 shows therelation between the frictional force and slip for a typlcal case on a dry road surdace. The transmited braking force reaches lts maximum value In shaded area A Thls ls also the control rangeof ABS. When a wheel ls locked,l.e. when there Is 100 % slip, the frictional forcewill normally belower than when a wheel Is rolling.

Consequently the ABS must control the brake pressure In the wheel brakecyllnder In such B manner that the sllp remains in the shaded area, because here the highest frictlonal force is available.

The amount of slip,with which there ls maximum frictlonal force, and the amount of frictional force Itself depend chlefly on the tires (type,treads, rubber composltion), the road surface (material, surface condition,wet, ice), the road speed and the slip angle of the wheels.

The ABS detects the frictional conditions between the tires and road surface prevalling at the moment It automaticallyadjusts to each change In road surface/tire relation and makes use of the highest coefficient of friction,without that the vehicle slips or skids because of wheel locking.

Non-unlform friction conditions between the separate wheels wlll be held under control just as also Instantaneous changes in the road surfaces,e.g. through patches of lce.

### DESIGN

ABS conslsts ofa control unit, hydraullc unit,speed sensors and a wire harness.Components are described separately below.


### Speed Sensors:

Each speed sensyr has agear wheel,which runspast the permanently magnetized edge of the speed sensor and isinstalled in the wheel hub.   
The rotary motlon of the wheels is recorded by Inductive sensors and an electric slgnal Is sent to the electronlc control unit.


### Electronic Control Unit:

The electronlc control unit is located In the car's slde member, see layout drawing on page 52/6.In a small muitl-channel computer acceleratlon, deceleration and slipfactors arederived from theelectricsignalsof the speed sensors,whlch are proportional to wheel velocity. By loglcal connection of these factors there are control commands for the electromagneticallyoperated valves inthe hydraulic unit.

The signal processing in the computer determines the control behavior of the system.The expected degree of dependabilityisbased on digital engineering with highly integrated cir cuitry.

The control unlt,contains electronlc monitoring circults, whlch control the function prior to each trlp and the ABS wire harness with equipment constantlyduring atrip.If the control unit detects a defect in the wire harness or electrical part of the equipment, themonltoring circult wlllswitch off the ABS and guarantee normal use of the brake system. An ABS indicator lampreports this condition to the driver.


### Hydraullc Unit:

The hydraulic unlt is located in theengine compartment and integrated in the conventional brake system.

To control the brake pressure in the wheel brake cyllnders, the brake hydraulic unit has three-way valves which permit three brake pressure conditlons.

Pressure bulld-up,pressure holding and pressure drop.These three pressure phases adapt themselves Inthesequencesand length to therequirementsof the desired control characterlstlc and power flow between the road surface and tires.

As soon as wheel deceleration or slip indicates the locking of a wheel,the brake pressure isfirst held. H the wheel still tends to lock, the pressure will be dropped so long until the wheel accelerates or the slip limit is exceeded. Afterwards the pressure Is ralsed agaln and the control phases begin from new.

Anelectrlcally driven return delivery pump returns the brake fiuid taken from the wheel brake cylinder while dropping the pressure to the appropriate brake circuit.

The pump Isdesigned asa two-plston pump so that the circults of a dual brake clrcult system remaln fully separated.


### Wlre Harness:

The control unit is connected with the speed sensors and electric part of the hydraulic unlt vlaa speclal wire harness forthesake of signalinput and orderoutput. These wires as well as electric power supply are integrated in the main wire harness.


### 2. Function and Checking ofABS Control'Lamp

The ABS control lamp lights up after switching the ignition on.   
The control lamp must go out ater starting the engine 1 ABS 1s okay.

The procedure is repeated each time the Ignltion Is swltched off and on.

The causes for faully display 一 control lamp does not llght up. does not go out or lghts up whlle driving (even sporadically)- can be determined by reading the fault memory with 日 BMWService Tester,refer to Car Electric/Electronlc Test Plan.

The control unlt automatically swltches lo "conventlonal brakes" In case olan electrlc or electronic fault In ABS.   
Thls means that the car can still be braked, but without regulation (the wheels could lock!).


### AUTOMATIC STABILITY CONTROL (ASC)

Description

AutomatlcStablllty Control (ASC) ls a control system to Improve active safety In that lt reduces the sllp of drivenwheels on roads wjth Insufficlent traction (prevents spinning of the wheels).

Itemploys Electronlc Engine Power Control (EML)and Digital Motor Electronics DME) for regulation.

The sensors of ABS are used to recognlze the speed of Indlvldual wheels.

ASC is Integrated with ABS In one control unit, but ls a completely independent system.

Whlle ABS exploits the maximum friction force while braking the car, this Is reached with ASC whlle accelerating.

Assoon asethe drlven wheels turn 0.25 km/h (0.15mph)faster than the non-driven wheels, ASC regulates the throttle valve position smaller via EML. In order to have fast regulation, thelgnltlon timing isretarded in steps or thereIs ignltion blend-out by DME. DMEalso adapts the fuel Injection signal to protect the engine and catalyst.

ASC Is combined with Engine Drag Torque Control (MSR),which prevents sliding of the driven wheels in case of sudden engine overrun.

Engine Drag Torque Control (MSR)

Agaln with the help of wheel sensors ASC recognizes the difference in speed between drlven (engine braked) wheels and non-driven (unbraked) wheels. ASC swltches off overrun cut-out when values are below the sllp limits.


### Displaying and Swltching Logic

The system Is swltched on after starting the engine and can be switched off as desired wlth a passive swltch button. ASC lamp is off with thesystem switched on.

Current regulation is indicated to the driver bya fiashing ASC lamp in the instrument cluster.

Ifthe ASC lamp lights up continuously, the system has been switched off on its own due lo an occured fault or ithad been swltched oft by hand.

Troubleshooting: See Car Electric/Electronic Test Plan.


### AUTOMATIC STABILITY CONTROL PLUS TRACTION (ASC +T

General

Thls system has the task of regulating the slip of driven wheels to the lowest possible value regardless ol road surface conditlons.

During regulation the engine torque is reduced with help of DME (lgnition timing control) and EML(throttle valve control).if thismeasure is not sufficlent, the driven wheel turning toofast is slowed down by the wheel brake via a hydraullc element.


### Dlsplaying and Swltching Logic

The system Isswitched on after starting the engine and can be swltched off as desired with 8 passive swltch button. ASC lamp ls off with the system switched on.

Current regulatlon is Indicated tothe driver by a flashing ASC lamp In the instrument cluster.

If the ASClamp lightsup continuously,the system has been switched off on its own due to an occured lault or was swltched off byhand.


### Ignition Timing Control by DME

Retarding the lgnition timing isanother measure forreduction of the engine iorque. In ASC mode (regulation) Digital Motor Electronics (DME) receives a dlgltal signal from ASC and retards the Ignitlon timing afterwards.

Troubleshooting: See Car Electric/Electronic Test Plan.

### 3612001 Replacing tireon front, back or spare wheel

Refer to operating instructions supplied with pertinent tiremountingmachine for correct mounting of tires. However,also make sure that the equipment isin perfect condition and that the wheel rim and tire are not damaged.

General tire removing mounting instructions

Removing:

Begin the removal of a tire at the valve.   
After pressing the tire off therim flange,   
remove balance weights,press tire bead into well and coat thoroughly with tiremounting paste   
Clean disc wheel thoroughly and inspect for damage before fitting the tire.   
The valve and valve insert must be replaced each time a tubeless tire is removed and installed.


> ⚠️ **Внимание:** 
> It will be necessary to loosen the bead at several points on the bead periphery from the inside and outside with the pressing-off horn before pressing off the tire.   
> lfit isvery difficult to press offthe tire,loosen tirefrom rim flange as wellas possible with the pressing-off horn and then apply a coatof tiremounting paste between the tire and rim flange.   
> Repeat this step around the entire tire periphery.   
> Then press of tire completely.


### Mounting:

Coat tire bead with tire mounting paste \*.   
Make sure tire is mounted on correct side, especially in case of asymmetric tires.   
The"outside"of these tires is marked.   
Mount tire with as little as possible stress on the beads,as otherwise there would be danger of damaging the tire.   
Have the tirebead -coming from the well 1 first jump over the hump of the rim shoulder.   
Build up pressure in steps while observing continuously.   
Maximum jumping pressure":3.3 bar.   
Ithe tire ls not seated on therimcorrectly,increasing theinflation pressure will not improve tire seating!   
Instead it will be necessary to press off both tire beads,apply another coat of mounting paste and then reinflate the tire.   
Only after the bead bears correctly on the rim shoulder should the pressure be slowly increased until the tire"seats".   
Maximum "seatingpressure":4.0 bar.   
Refer to Service Information of Group 36 for approved tires and tire sizes as well as special equipment.


### 36-12/2

![](images/376bd4ea6546cbb153b19a6ad77c0aac0ae46ab39af51b8324509cfe1f8036de.webp)

Mounting tires with a mounting machine:

Unscrew valve and deflate tire.   
Press off bead from rim flange all around on outside and inside using pressing-off horn of machine.   
Itirebeadsfittoo tight,first only ioosen tire from flange at several points with thepressingof hornprior to the actual pressing-off operation.   
Push both tirebeads into rimwell completely until they are loose.   
Pull off balance weights on rim and clean rim toremove large pieces of dirt.   
Coat tire beads with mounting paste   
Clamp wheel on mounting machine.   
Narrow rim shoulder always faces up. Let mounting machine run backa short dlstance (counterclockwise) so that the tire bead can slide fully on to the mounting finger.   
Then let mounting machine run forward (clockwise) a short distance.   
In so doing always check whether the bottom bead is in the welland the tire is givenenough time tomove.   
Stop the machine and let it run back slightly if the bead jams. Swing mounting pillar into position or fold and let it engage.   
Adjust mounting head, whereby it must be pressed on the rim edge fuly and turn down the lever for the clamp fixture;normally the distance of the mounting head will set in automatically.   
Valve should be about 10 cm to the right of the mounting head.   
Lifttire bead over mounting finger using tire irons.   
It is recommended to use coated or shrink-fit hose covered tire irons for light alloy rims.

Hot galvanized and galvanized sheet meial us used toa greater extent lor components of tho body. whlch areespeclally subject to corroslon.

Conformance wlth the following points ls necessary when working with these parts. Thewelding smoke contalns poisonous zinc oxlde, so thal especlally goo-d extractlon isnecessary In the welding bay.

A coat ol spot welding paste can beapplled for better sealing. Inert gas weldlng should be preterred to autogen welding Inareas nol accessible lor reslstance spot weldlng. because ol the lower heat dlsperslon.   
Machining or torming ol galvanized sheet metal In warm state is normal.

Align,grind down and tin out visible Jolnts as normally.

### 1. Cutting Out Damaged Parts:

Determine the location of jointsinaccordance with the replacement part before starting the operation.   
Cut out the damaged part roughly within these joints.

Caution!

Be careful notto damage sheet metal underneath!

Remove sealing compound,anti-drumming compound and,ifapplicable paint to neutralize the joints. Drill off welding spots. Whendrillingoff,makesuretatthedrilledholesare produced in the cut out part. Do not drillin theremaining connection flanges.

Grind off welded seams carefully witha disc grinder.Heat brazed connections with an autogen torch! Do not overheat! Take offscrap metal. Remove remaining spongy brazing solder with a steel brush.Straightenand grindoffalljoint surlaces thoroughly.

2. Installing New Parts:

Prepare joints in accordance with relevant repair instructions.

Repairs to suspension points for engine or transmisslon and running gear parts must be carried out on a straightening bench using the set of attachments for acertain vehicle type. Other attachments are also available lor variousbody parts. Check curvature and dimensions of windshield and rear window by installing the original windows. Refer to relevant drawings for gaps in doors, engine hood and trunk lid.

Coat joints required for resistance spot welding with zinc dust paint Only remove protective paint from galvanized replacement parts. Drill 8 mm dia. holes in joints not accessible for spot welding tongs,using the spacing of drilled-off spotsand plug spot weld these joints.

Produce inert gas welded seams according to the cut-out part

Produce brazed joints with heat dispersion limited to a minimum and without overheating. Joining methods which deviate from standard production will be described in therepair instructions. Grind down welded seams on visible outside surfaces.

>
> All welded seams sealed offwith body sealing compound in original state must be sealed off again thoroughly immediately afterrepairing. Replacedamagedanti-drumming compound. New sheet metal parts or cavities,seams, creases and folds formed by the new sheet metal parts must be sealed with a body sealing compound immediately.

### 4161 014 Adjusting hoodlid

Note:   
The lids and doors are aligned in the body shell and bolted into place.   
During subsequent movement, unpainted surfaces become exposed.   
These must be touched up in the appropriate color of paint.


### Open hood lid.

Unfasten left and right screws (1)in such a way that the hood lid can bemoved.

Loosen screw (2) on left and right with special tool 41 6 100 to enable the hood lid to be moved and adjusted.

![](images/715d51c9198a41d4b06662e91ab420564bd7aa9e87b12a1c5586f3bf313bc7f2.webp)

Note: Screws (1) for height adjustment of hood lid. Screw (2) for angle adjustment of hood lid.

![](images/62d9a16fdc155671696fc51f3ae90b4c8f7bff6b1d99a7a43744790b1235c464.webp)

R 410003

Summary of hood lid adjustment: Screw (1) = height adjustment Screw(2) =angle adjustment Screws （3) = longitudinal adjustment

Loosen screws (3) on left and right sides to enable these to be Inserted in the hood lid.

Note:   
Screw (3)for longitudinal adjustment of hood lid.

![](images/4032537ee341bd8f8351f676272cc136f26c45e051cdd1501071e941ae5f1b07.webp)

Carefully close hood lid.

Caution!   
Hood lid must not make contact with side panels,front trim (bumper) and the headlight pod covers.

A 410004

Height of the hood lid:   
The hood lid should be approx. 1 mm lower than the side panels.

2 Open clips on air guide cover for radiator by twisting.

The distance between hood lid and side panels and to front trim (bumper) should feature a uniform width of gap all round. The hood lid should be approx. mm deeper than the side panels.

Adjustment dimensions: refer to gaps for doors hood lid and trunk lid.

3. Insert a screwdriver in the groove at the marked points.Twist screwdriver in order to release the lock.

Align hood lid to side panels and to front trim (bumper).

Open hood lid and tighten loosened screws.

Check setting and repeat if necessary.

Check setting of hood lid locks and adjust if necessary.

Remove alr guide forradiator and unclip Bowden cable for right hood lid lock.

### 51-31 Instructions on cementing windows

Front and rear windows are cemented to body (positive connection). This improves the torsional strength of the vehicle. Conformance with the following procedures is necessary to ensure windows are correctly cemented

Note:

When using Sika Tack 1 Ultrafast (hot treatment). the cement must be heated in the cartridge oven" to 80°C.

)pen rear end of aluminum membrane before placing cartridge in oven.


### Removal:

Cement bead is cut through using an electric cutter\* with oscillating blade\*. as far as possible without damaging paint on the body aperture. When cutting out the window, wear protective goggles and gloves. Damaged paint finish in body openings must be touched up with BMWEP prime filler\*. Large areas of damage must be ground down to base metal and coated with BMW EP prime filler (2K) (layer thickness 30 1r1 40 μm).If a complete buildup of paint is required in the visible area, masking must be stripped off the primed cement flange before application of top coat.

Preparation for assembly:

Note:

When using Sika Tack Ultrafast (hot treatment):   
Before applying the cement, itmust first be heated in a cartridge oven\* to 80°℃.   
Sealed cement containers can be reheated several times and they remain stable for approx. 10 hours at 80°C.

The inside edge of the window is coated with a glass ceramic layer impermeable to UV light to protect the cement bead. A thin coat of primer is applied by brush to the glass ceramic surface (repair kit)\*. Primer must be allowed to breathe for at least 10 minutes.

The body aperture is also coated with a thin layer of primer, requiring 10 minutes to air-dry. For cementing,only use the 1-component polyurethane cements(Sikaflex 255FC for cold treatment or Sika Tack Ultrafast for hot treatment)\*.The cement is applied to the window with a cartridge press (compressed air or electrically operated)\*.

If a cement other than one approved by BMW is used,radio reception is seriously impaired. The heating filaments also act as antennas.

Mounting:

Caution!

The car can be towed without a windshield or rear window.

To prevent a pressure buildup inside the car when the doors are closed, one side window should be open.

Cement hardens by reaction with humidity at room temperature.

Theminimum hardening timeisachievedat 22°C and 38% relative humidityrefer to table. The vehicle must not be subjected to one-sided loads during the minimumhardening time (for example one wheel on kerb, lifting platform etc.).Maneuvering inside the workshop is still permitted.

Caution!

iafety instruction after cementing (windshield with passenger airbag):

To ensure that the 'passenger airbag" restraint system functions perfectly (support of airbag against windshield),all occupantsmust drive with seatbelts fastened until the minimum hardening time (refer to table) is reached after the windshield has been cemented.

### 520 DIAGNOSING DAMAGE OFBELT SYSTEM INTEGRATED IN FAONT SEAT AFTER ACCIDENT

In the Interest of occupants' salety no other repairs are permitted than those described below!Damaged components must bereplaced!

Relerence must be taken to the following criterla when diagnosing damage.

Backrest play,measured at upper belt outlet point perpendicular to the backrest 二 max. 20 mm.

Measuring maximum backrest play:   
Set seatto hlghest helght posltlon and backrest to most uprig ht position.   
Press backrest agalnst front stopwith force of about 200 N.   
Measure distance perpendicular to backrest fromupper belt outlet polnt towindshleld and note value.   
Now press backrest agalnst rear stop with force of about 200 N and agaln measure distance perpendlcular to backrest fromupper belt outlet point to windshield. The diference of both measured dlstances is the backrest play.

Bending of belt anchors on seat frame {for both lower belt points) towards seat cushion, Le. belt lock bears on seal cushion.

Belt anchors may be bent back to thelr original positlon without effecting the vehicle'ssalety.

All dlsturbances such asnolse, selzure, hesitation, etc. aswell as not reaching the final posltions for all seat control functions.

Front-end Colllslon

Refer to the dlagram for sequence of procedure. Indicators forthe stress of the seat atter a front-end colllslon.are chlelly the belt anchors on the seat frame. ltcan berecognlzed on them,whether forces had been exerted to the belt system. This will be noticed on the bending of anchors towards the seat cushion and will always make It necessary to Inspect the seat outside of thecar.

Rear-end Collslon

Refer to the diagram forsequence of procedure. Thechiet indicator for stress of the seat-integrated belt system aftera rear-end collision is excessive backrestplay. This point must be glven special attention when checking.

Slde Colllslon, Oblique Collision and Rollover

Proceed as described for the front-end colllsion If belt anchors on the seat frame are bent (belt ock bears on seat cushion).

Proceed as described for the rear-end collision ibelt anchors are not bent,but conslderable backrest play Is noticed.   
I the seat is within the zone In which the car is deformed, replace the damaged parts or components.

### BATTERY CARE AND MAINTENANCE

The electrolyte level of present low-malntenance batteries should be checked at least annually and corrected to themax. mark speclfied by the battery suppller with distilled water when necessary.

Dlscharging by the power consumption of control units even in standby mode Is added lo the natural self-discharging ola battery due to the Increaslngnumber of control unlts used In cars today. The batterles of cars in storage should be recharged at the latest every slx weekstomaintain the service lifeandavold excesslve dlscharging(refer to battery recharging calender).The time for self-dischargingdepends on the car model and oqulpment.


### Charging Battery:

If a standard or fast charger (e.g. Bosch SL 24 90\*) Is used to charge a battery, the battery must be dlsconnected from the car's electrical system and removed in order to avold damage to palnt finlshes and uphoistery by the escaping gas.   
Excesslvely discharged batterles could be damaged or destroyed by the very hlgh Inltlal current (hlgh temperature).   
The battery can remaln connected when using an electronlc charger (e.g. Slemens V8 80).   
The electronlcs deos not permit crltical peak voltage.   
An electronlc charger also charges anexcesslvely discharged battery with reduced current untll a certaln baslc voltage Is reached.   
Refer to Service Infomation 61 08881 there Is doubt as to whether or not the battery charger In the workshop ls sultable.


### Important!

Always first measure the open clrcult voltage before charging a battery Installed In the car. Iths voltagels10V or less,t cannot be excluded that oneor more cells are faulty or that the battery asa whole Is already pre-damaged.   
In thls case IlIsalways necessary to remove the battery as escaping gas whlle chargIng could damage Interior equipment.   
Altempt toregenerate the faultycelswlth low charging current.   
Romove plugs from the separate celis In the Interest of safety.

Also reler to page 61-21/1.


### Testing Battery:

An objectlve statement on the charged conditlon of a battery is only possible by way of aload test wlth cold testing current. Thls test can be carrled out wlth a battery tester, fer example

Bosch T12220\* or preferrably with Bosch T12 200\*.

Addltlonal Informatlon on load tests ls contalned In the pertinent operating Instructlons (also reler to page 61-20/1).

The acld denslty of a battery can also be used to determine the charged condilon. Thls test, however,ls notasposltlve due to the design-orlentated dlsperslon range of acid denslty e.g.charged standard battery verslon =acld density 1.28kg/ltr. -troplc verslon =acid density 1.23kg/ltr.).

There ls hlgh current load of approx. 200 A, wlth electronlc evaluatlon of the voltage curve during and after load. Thls test Is presently the most dependable method of evaluating the charged condltion and physlcal battey condltion (such as cell shorts,sulphatation).

Start the test as described In the operating Instructlons.

### 6120 CHECKING BATTERY IN OPEN CIACUIT CURAENT TEST

If the battery Is okay after the high current test, battery discharging could be caused by excessive open circult current consumptlon.


### Before Open Circult Current Test:

Swltch al consumers off whlch can be swltched off(lgnltlon,Inslde lights,reading lamps,seat heating,addltional heater,   
additlonal ventilator,telephone,etc.).   
Shut the glovebox,trunk lld and engine hood.   
Vehicle must have been unused at least 3 hours.

Keep to the following procedures so that posslbly selzing relays do not fall.


### Connecting Ammeter:

Connect the posltive lead of the ammeter to the disconnected ground connection. Connect the ground lead of the ammeter to body ground.

Remove the shrink-fit hose on the body end of the battery ground lead on the batterles. Clip on a cable wlth an allgatorclip at thls polnt (Hirschmann AK 2S cllp together with test leads,red = Order No. 61 1 472and black = Order No.61 1474).

Cllp asecond cable on body ground. Close, lockand arrest (double-lock) the drlver's door and front passenger's.

The trunk lld remains open.

Disconnect the battery ground lead with connected alligator cllp on the ground connection polnt carefully5minutesafter the locking step and bend Itaway. Static current now flows only via the multimeter.

Slmulatlon of the closed car by presslng the trunk llght swltch on the striker.   
Read static current value on the multimeter.

Ifthe statlc current ls more than

it can be assumed that a hidden consumer is loading the battery. The hidden consumer can be pinpointed by pulling off fuses,possibly relays and control units one after the other.

When testing and possibly troubleshooting have been concluded, the multlmeter must beremoved In reverse order of Installation S0 that the memorles o theradlo,on-board computerand varlous control units are not cancelled.

Static Current Test In Carswith Burglar Alarm:

In order to beable to measure theactual statlc current, the trunk contact must bepressed 5 mlnutes after the locking step.

The trunk contact must not be released Immediately afterreadingthestatic cur-rent, because then the burglaralarm horn would be active. This excessive cur-rent for the selected measuring range ofthe multimeter could destroy the In- strument, but at least the Installed fuse.

The ground lead must always be reconnected in reverse order of disconnection, In order to be able to deactlvate and unlock the car correctly.


### 6121011 REPLACING BATTEAY

Always conform with the following points when car Is fitted with two batteries.   
Check the conditlon of both batterles In a hlgh current test.   
Dlsconnect the batterles trom the car's olectrical system and check the batterles separately In hlgh current test.   
Replace both batteries,lf after charging the hlgh current tests show acharged condition ol less than 70%and starting power of less than 75%.

When replacing adelective battery,the second battery must also be replaced. When replacing batteries, ensure that both batteries are of the same make.

Important!

If both batterlesare not replaced at the same time,theolder battery could damage the otherbattery due to thedlfferent degree of sulphatatlon. In other words the batteries would discharge on thelr own to 8 certalndegree.

On vehicles with an approach angle adjustment facility,theignition switched offand the wiper blade installed,check the clearance between the adjusting screw （1）and the push rod (2) - this should be A = 0- 0.2 mm.

lfthe approach angle is defective,the wiper armmust be turned into the correct position using special tool009.220.

fold-away position

### DESCRIPTION OF REFRIGERANT CIRCUIT FUNCTION

Afterswitching on the alr conditioner the retrlgerant clrcult Is aclivated In Ihat the solenold clutch recelves current.This produces poslive connectlon between the pulley and armature clutch plate and the compressor isdriven.

The compressor, majorcomponent of the system, Increases the pressure of refrigerant vapors. Refrigorant vapors are drawn In on the Intake slde of the compressor. The refrigerant lscompressed,whereby the vapor temperature rises.The high pressure vapors pass via a hlgh pressure plpe to 日 condenser located on the face of the engine radlator.The hotrefrlgerant ls cooied off by wind fromdrlvingand an addltlonal lan. Refgerant vaporscondense and turn Into liquld when reaching the dewpolnt temperature.Thehighpressurlzedrefrigerant lsdellvered lo thedrler.Thedrlerremovesmoisturefrom the refrigorant andsomelimes alsoaclds, but tho latter only fn the amount o1 6to10 grams for.R 12or 10to 16 grams forR134 asystems.

Refrigerant continues on to the expansion valve from the drier. The expansion valve makes up a point of separatlon In the system.The expanslon valve meters therefrigerant.Volume of refrigerant Is controlled by the temperature and pressure at the outlet o thevaporator.The relrigetant evaporales andcools off conslderably in theevaporator. The tresh alr -respectively circulaied alr- lowing past tho cold evaporator,wlth blowsupport, Iscooled accordingly and delivered Into the passenger compartmenl vla nozzles.

The evaporated refrigerant is drawn in again bythe compressor,whereby tho refrigerant circult 1s completed.

Molsture from the fresh or clrculated alr, flowing past the evaporator. condenses on lhe cold fins.The condensation on theevaporatorisdischarged outdoors vlarubber hoses on thetransmlssion tunnel and could cause apuddle o1 up to 200 ml underneath a parked car depending on the atmospheric molsture. Thls Iscompletely normal and does not Indicate aleak.

lt could happen that the condensation wator freezes on the fins of ihe evaporator. An vaporalor lemperature sensor prevents the fomatlon of lce In'that isswitches tho compressor ll1 2 C. The compressorls swltched on agaln wllh a revorsing rangeof 2C.A salety wltch (hlgh or low pressure pressostal) swltches the alr conditloner oll when pressure ls too high or too low.Thlsprevents damage to the alr conditloner. A modium pressure pressostal swltches the second stage of an addition fan on al a pressure of about 18 bar.

In thismannerthe compressors not switched ofl andon so oflen, as the maximum hlgh prossure 1s not reached \$0 tast.

### OPERATION OFLOCK SENSOR

The lock sonsor consists ofa control unit and speed sensor (lock sensor) on the AC compressor.

Thls lock sensor ls installed only inmodels wlth theM70engine （750,850)becauso the AC compressor and water pump are drlven by the same rlbbed drive belt. H the ribbed drive balt tears orjumps olf of the pulley when the compressor locks, tho engine cooling system would also fall.Thlslspreventedby theelectronlcs of the lock sonsor control unit.It continuouslymonltors engine speed and compressor speed and Immedlately swltches themagnetic clutch o1 the compressoroft when there lsmore than30 %sllp.This control unlt also monltors coolant temperature and at first tmes the compressor In case of overheating and switches it of laler If the temperature rlses further.

After starting the engine and exceeding an engine speed of 600 rpm for the first time the control unlt Is activated,the compressor ls swltched on,engine speed ls continuously compared with compressor speed and coolant temperature Ismeasured. I during ameasuring perlod of200 mlllsseconds sllp Is recognlzed once at hlgh speed or sllpls recognlzed three times at lowspeed, the compressor will be switched olf.


### Important!

The compressor can only be swltched onagaln lf the engine ls started agaln. In caso o1 fault and when amechanical defect ol the compressor cannot be lound, check whether brief sllp has occurred whlle driving through apuddle(wetribbeddrivebelt).

Monltoring ofthe coolant temperature takes place paralleltomonltoring of slp.llthe coolant temperature exceods tho117' C mark wlth rlslng tendency, the compressor wll be tlmed,I.e. the magnetic clutch of the compressor wlli be swltched off 1or 20 seconds every 40 seconds. I thls measure causes the coolant temperalure to drop below 114 C, the compressor will agaln bo switched oncontinuously.However, Ifi rlses again to 120C,the compressor wlllbe switched off untlllIs below Ihe 114 C mark.
